title: Hindenburg disaster
summary: The Hindenburg, a hydrogen-filled rigid airship, arrived at Lakehurst on 6 May 1937 after crossing the Atlantic from Frankfurt. During the docking procedure with the mooring mast, the airship caught fire and burned rapidly, destroying the structure. Thirty-five passengers and crew plus one person on the ground were killed. The disaster shattered public confidence in giant rigid airships.
probable_cause: Hydrogen fuel ignited during mooring attempt at Lakehurst. Exact cause of ignition remains disputed.

factors.evidence: Hydrogen-filled airship burned rapidly during docking with mooring mast
The hydrogen-filled airship caught fire and was destroyed during its attempt to dock
Airship structure destroyed, marking the abrupt end of the airship era

events.text: Hindenburg crossed Atlantic from Frankfurt and passed over Boston on morning of May 6
Airship was hours behind schedule and diverted to wait for afternoon thunderstorms to pass
Directed back to Lakehurst to make landing after being notified storms had passed
The hydrogen-filled airship caught fire and was destroyed during its attempt to dock with its mooring mast at Naval Air Station Lakehurst, causing 35 fatalities among the 97 people on board

notes: Exact cause of ignition remains disputed
Multiple theories proposed for ignition source

title: Sabena OO-AUB Ostend crash
summary: A Junkers Ju 52/3m SABENA flight from Munich to London scheduled to stop at Frankfurt, Brussels and Ostend diverted to Stene Aerodrome near Ostend due to bad weather. At 14:47 local time the aircraft struck the chimney of a brick factory and crashed, bursting into flames, killing all 12 on board. A Belgian official enquiry concluded that a passenger, Grand Duchess Cecilie, gave birth during flight, and the pilot was attempting emergency landing because of this medical emergency.
probable_cause: A Belgian official enquiry concluded the pilot was attempting to land at the aerodrome despite poor weather conditions because one of the passengers, the Hereditary Grand Duchess Cecilie who was 8-months pregnant, gave birth during the flight. The aircraft struck a brick factory chimney at 2:47 p.m., causing the crash.

factors.evidence: bad weather caused the flight to divert to Stene Aerodrome instead of the scheduled stop at Ostend Airport
one passenger, Grand Duchess Cecilie, gave birth during flight which was the reason pilot was attempting to land despite poor weather
Aircraft hit the chimney of a brick factory and crashed at 2:47 p.m. local time

events.text: Medical emergency develops as passenger Grand Duchess Cecilie who was 8-months pregnant gives birth during flight
Pilot diverts from scheduled route and attempts emergency landing at Stene Aerodrome in bad weather due to birth on board
Aircraft hit the chimney of a brick factory and crashed, bursting into flames

notes: No formal accident investigation report cited
Medical emergency as primary cause based on official inquiry conclusion
Records show 11 passengers and crew on board plus newborn remains found = 12 total
